factual_claims.claim: LLMs are currently trained to identify themselves as language models, but it is unclear if they truly understand this or reliably act on it.
Performance on situational awareness tasks is only partially predicted by general knowledge benchmarks like MMLU.
LLMs can be prompted to demonstrate situational awareness, such as knowing their own identity, training data, and deployment context.
Chat-finetuned models generally perform better on situational awareness tasks than their base model counterparts.
Situating prompts (reminding the model it is an LLM) significantly improve performance on situational awareness benchmarks.
Current LLMs struggle to accurately count the number of tokens in their own input, indicating limited introspective capability regarding their internal architecture.
Large language models exhibit a measurable bias toward guessing they are in a testing or evaluation environment when presented with ambiguous text.
Increasing model scale (parameter count) significantly improves the ability of LLMs to perform situational inference tasks.
Models perform significantly better on tasks where the target words are provided (given) compared to tasks where they must be generated (not-given).
Base models often outperform chat-tuned models on specific situational awareness benchmarks.
